content.content: 1 # Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. content.text:
I graded the six new test files and the changed `runToExit` line in the smoke test. **The work fails your bar (overall 9, no item under 7): overall is 8, duplication scores 6 and tests scores 7.** `npm test` passes all 149 tests, and the project root has no stray `bookings.json` afterwards. I could not check for leftover temp folders because permission for that command was denied. Each test makes its own temp folder and removes it afterwards, so leftovers are unlikely.

The smoke-test change is correct: the 'close' event at `/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.smoke.test.mjs:54` fires only after stdout and stderr have been fully read. The shared harness's `runToExit` does the same, and its timeout reports 'still running' instead of hanging.

**Duplicated helpers that belong in the shared harness or `fake-dom.mjs`**
- "Kill the server and wait for it to exit" is written three times: `server.startup.test.mjs:18` (`waitExit`), `server.datafile.test.mjs:185` (`restart`), and inline at `server.routing.test.mjs:221-222`.
- Two chunked-upload helpers do the same job: `chunkedPost` (`server.rules.test.mjs:45`) and `chunkedUpload` (`server.routing.test.mjs:143`).
- `expectError` (`server.rules.test.mjs:21`) is the harness `assertError` plus a label. It exists because `assertError` takes no message.
- The JSON content-type header is defined again as `JSON_H` (`server.datafile.test.mjs:16`) and as `json` (`server.startup.test.mjs:92`), although the harness exports `JSON_HEADERS`.
- The same three "rejected data file" assertions appear three times in `server.datafile.test.mjs` (lines 52-54, 64-66, 78-80).
- `page.behaviour.test.mjs` rewrites helpers that `page-list.test.mjs` and `page.test.mjs` already have: `bk` matches `booking`, `setup` matches `withList`, and `submit` exists in both.
- Outside the graded lines: `server.smoke.test.mjs:12-95` still carries its own copy of the whole harness.

**Assertions in loops with no message saying which case failed**
- `server.routing.test.mjs:47`, `:74`, `:240` call `assertError` with no label.
- At `server.routing.test.mjs:88` the label `name` is built but only passed on the HEAD branch, not to `assertError`.
- `server.startup.test.mjs:38`: `assertOneLine` is not told which PORT value failed.
- `page.behaviour.test.mjs:200-204`, `:315-316` and `:366-369` have no labels.

**Timing and flakiness**
- `server.startup.test.mjs:101` waits a fixed 100 ms. A late write to stdout would slip through, so the test passes when it should fail. It can never fail falsely.
- `server.startup.test.mjs:59` and `:67` check that a port is free, then start the server on it. If something grabs the port in between, the test fails instead of skipping. This risk is small and accepted.
- `rules:53` and `routing:153` parse the reply with `JSON.parse` inside the 'end' handler. A reply that is not JSON throws an uncaught error instead of rejecting the promise.
- `startServer` (`server-harness.mjs:39`) has no timeout of its own, so a server that never prints its listening line hangs until the test runner times out.

I found no tests that depend on each other: every test boots its own server in its own temp folder. The exact-value checks on spec messages and bodies are strong throughout. The tests catch real near-misses, such as counting characters instead of bytes, `<` instead of `<=` on the time boundaries, and NBSP or tab padding in the Content-Type header.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 8 — clean split by concern; a few tests do too many jobs (routing "query is cut") and `change` is declared async with no await
naming: 8 — mostly clear; terse names like `bk`, `kids`, `B`, `file3`, `JSON_H`, and `a`/`b`/`f`/`g` in datafile 101-117
duplication: 6 — three copies of kill-and-wait, two chunked uploaders, a second assertError, re-declared header constants, page helpers copied from page-list/page.test
size: 9 — every file under 420 lines and every function under 50
errors: 8 — JSON.parse inside 'end' handlers throws uncaught; startServer has no timeout of its own
tests: 7 — strong exact-value checks and near-miss coverage, but several unlabelled asserts in loops, one fixed sleep, one check tied to the file layout, and invisible characters written raw in the source
security: 10 — no secrets; all temp folders come from mkdtemp
leftovers: 9 — no console.log or commented-out code; a small formatting slip at page.behaviour:174
